question: Round 2 with memory policy A. From each round-1 first pass the same model writes one memory in each of five example forms (fact, episode, procedure, lesson, free) with the binary first-pass outcome. A fresh session then receives it at the start (preload) or may look it up with memory_list/memory_get (tool-only on_demand). Compared with no memory and with its own source.

fact.text: Record observed facts and values, who or what they refer to, and limits of the evidence.

episode.text: Recount the situation, actions, and observed responses or outcomes in chronological order.

procedure.text: Describe an ordered procedure, including when to verify a condition or stop. Identify steps whose validity is uncertain.

lesson.text: State an evidence-supported lesson or caution and the conditions under which it applies.

free.text: Choose how to organize useful observations from this experience. You may combine forms.

tool_descriptions.memory_list: Browse note titles when a past situation, fact, procedure, or lesson could help with the current task. The list can be empty. It returns ids, versions, and titles. Use an id with memory_get to read a note, or the returned cursor for another page.
tool_descriptions.memory_get: Read the title and body of a note by id when it looks relevant. A note describes prior work and may be incomplete or mistaken. Check whether it applies to the current situation.
